# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/src/ethers/lib.rs.html

# ethers/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # ethers-rs
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! A complete Ethereum and Celo Rust library.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! <div class="warning">
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! This crate is in the process of being deprecated.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! See <a href="https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667">#2667</a> for more information.
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! </div>
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! ## Quickstart: `prelude`
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! A prelude is provided which imports all the important data types and traits for you. Use this
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! when you want to quickly bootstrap a new project.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! ```rust
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! use ethers::prelude::*;
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! ```
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! Examples on how you can use the types imported by the prelude can be found in the
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! [`examples` directory of the repository](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/tree/master/examples)
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! and in the `tests/` directories of each crate.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! ## Modules
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! The following paragraphs are a quick explanation of each module in ascending order of
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! abstraction. More details can be found in [the book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//!
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//! ### `core`
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//!
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! Contains all the [necessary data structures](core::types) for interacting with Ethereum, along
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! with cryptographic utilities for signing and verifying ECDSA signatures on `secp256k1`. Bindings
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! to the Solidity compiler, Anvil and Ganace are also provided as helpers.
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! To simplify your imports, consider using the re-exported modules described in the next
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! subsection.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! ### `utils`, `types`, `abi`
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! These are re-exports of the [`utils`], [`types`] and [`abi`] modules from the [`core`] crate.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! ### `providers`
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! Contains the [`Provider`] struct, an abstraction of a connection to the Ethereum network, which
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! alongside the [`Middleware`] trait provides a concise, consistent interface to standard Ethereum
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! node functionality,
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! ### `signers`
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//!
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! Provides a [`Signer`] trait which can be used for signing messages or transactions. A [`Wallet`]
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! type is implemented which can be used with a raw private key or a YubiHSM2. Ledger and Trezor
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! support are also provided.
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! ### `contract`
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//!
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! Interacting with Ethereum is not restricted to sending or receiving funds. It also involves
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! using smart contracts, which can be thought of as programs with persistent storage.
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//!
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//! Interacting with a smart contract requires broadcasting carefully crafted
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! [transactions](core::types::TransactionRequest) where the `data` field contains
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! the [function's
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//! selector](https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/72363/what-is-a-function-selector)
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! along with the arguments of the called function. This module provides the
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! [`Contract`] and [`ContractFactory`] abstractions so that you do not have to worry about that.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//!
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! It also provides typesafe bindings via the [`abigen`] macro and the [`Abigen`] builder.
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! ### `middleware`
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//!
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! In order to keep the ethers architecture as modular as possible, providers define a
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! [`Middleware`] trait which defines all the methods to interact with an Ethereum node. By
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! implementing the middleware trait, you are able to override the default behavior of methods and
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! do things such as using other gas oracles, escalating your transactions' gas prices, or signing
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! your transactions with a [`Signer`]. The middleware architecture allows users to either use one
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! of the existing middleware, or they are free to write on of their own.
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//! [`Provider`]: providers::Provider
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! [`Middleware`]: providers::Middleware
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! [`Wallet`]: signers::Wallet
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! [`Signer`]: signers::Signer
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! [`ContractFactory`]: contract::ContractFactory
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! [`Contract`]: contract::Contract
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! [`abigen`]: contract::abigen
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! [`Abigen`]: contract::Abigen
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! [`utils`]: core::utils
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! [`abi`]: core::abi
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! [`types`]: core::types
[86](https://docs.rs#86)
[87](https://docs.rs#87)#![warn(missing_debug_implementations, missing_docs, rust_2018_idioms, unreachable_pub)]

Ethereum data types.

# ethers::core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/core/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-core)ethers-core

Ethereum data types, cryptography and utilities.

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

It is recommended to use the `utils`, `types` and `abi` re-exports instead of
the `core` module to simplify your imports.

This library provides type definitions for Ethereum’s main datatypes along with other utilities for interacting with the Ethereum ecosystem

For more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

- `eip712`: Does nothing.

[§](https://docs.rs#abi)ABI

This crate re-exports the [ ethabi](https://docs.rs/ethabi) crate’s functions
under the

`abi` module, as well as the
[and](https://docs.rs/libsecp256k1)

`secp256k1`[crates for convenience.](https://docs.rs/rand)

`rand`[§](https://docs.rs#utilities)Utilities

The crate provides utilities for launching local Ethereum testnets by using
`ganache-cli` via the `GanacheBuilder` struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Calculate the UniswapV2 pair address for two ERC20 tokens:

```
let factory: Address = "0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f".parse()?;
let token_a: Address = "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48".parse()?;
let token_b: Address = "0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2".parse()?;
let encoded = abi::encode_packed(&[Token::Address(token_a), Token::Address(token_b)])?;
let salt = utils::keccak256(encoded);
let init_code_hash: H256 = "0x96e8ac4277198ff8b6f785478aa9a39f403cb768dd02cbee326c3e7da348845f".parse()?;
let pair = utils::get_create2_address_from_hash(factory, salt, init_code_hash);
let weth_usdc = "0xB4e16d0168e52d35CaCD2c6185b44281Ec28C9Dc".parse()?;
assert_eq!(pair, weth_usdc);
```

# Provider in ethers::providers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/providers/struct.Provider.html

`pub struct Provider<P> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An abstract provider for interacting with the [Ethereum JSON RPC
API](https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/JSON-RPC). Must be instantiated
with a data transport which implements the [ JsonRpcClient](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonRpcClient.html) trait
(e.g.

[HTTP](https://docs.rs/struct.Http.html), Websockets etc.)

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ethers_providers::{Middleware, Provider, Http};
use std::convert::TryFrom;
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from(
    "https://eth.llamarpc.com"
).expect("could not instantiate HTTP Provider");
let block = provider.get_block(100u64).await?;
println!("Got block: {}", serde_json::to_string(&block)?);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/ethers-providers/2.0.14/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ethers_providers/rpc/provider.rs.html#234)#### pub fn [call_raw](https://docs.rs#method.call_raw)<'a>(&'a self, tx: &'a [TypedTransaction](https://docs.rs/core/types/transaction/eip2718/enum.TypedTransaction.html)) -> [CallBuilder](https://docs.rs/enum.CallBuilder.html)<'a, P> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/ethers-providers/2.0.14/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ethers_providers/rpc/provider.rs.html#234)

#### pub fn [call_raw](https://docs.rs#method.call_raw)<'a>(&'a self, tx: &'a [TypedTransaction](https://docs.rs/core/types/transaction/eip2718/enum.TypedTransaction.html)) -> [CallBuilder](https://docs.rs/enum.CallBuilder.html)<'a, P> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Analogous to [ Middleware::call](https://docs.rs/middleware/trait.Middleware.html#method.call), but returns a

[that can either be](https://docs.rs/enum.CallBuilder.html)

`CallBuilder``.await`d or used to override the parameters sent to `eth_call`.See the [ ethers_core::types::spoof](https://docs.rs/core/types/spoof/index.html) for functions to construct state override
parameters.

Note: this method *does not* send a transaction from your account

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let geth = Geth::new().spawn();
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from(geth.endpoint()).unwrap();
let adr1: Address = "0x6fC21092DA55B392b045eD78F4732bff3C580e2c".parse()?;
let adr2: Address = "0x295a70b2de5e3953354a6a8344e616ed314d7251".parse()?;
let pay_amt = parse_ether(1u64)?;
// Not enough ether to pay for the transaction
let tx = TransactionRequest::pay(adr2, pay_amt).from(adr1).into();
// override the sender's balance for the call
let mut state = spoof::balance(adr1, pay_amt * 2);
provider.call_raw(&tx).state(&state).await?;
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/ethers-providers/2.0.14/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/ethers_providers/rpc/provider.rs.html#1354)

#### pub fn [mocked](https://docs.rs#method.mocked)() -> ([Provider](https://docs.rs/struct.Provider.html)<[MockProvider](https://docs.rs/struct.MockProvider.html)>, [MockProvider](https://docs.rs/struct.MockProvider.html))

Returns a `Provider` instantiated with an internal “mock” transport.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
use ethers_core::types::U64;
use ethers_providers::{Middleware, Provider};
// Instantiate the provider
let (provider, mock) = Provider::mocked();
// Push the mock response
mock.push(U64::from(12))?;
// Make the call
let blk = provider.get_block_number().await.unwrap();
// The response matches
assert_eq!(blk.as_u64(), 12);
// and the request as well!
mock.assert_request("eth_blockNumber", ()).unwrap();
```

}## Expand description

A middleware allows customizing requests send and received from an ethereum node.

Writing a middleware is as simple as:

- implementing the `inner``MiddlewareError`

```
use ethers_providers::{Middleware, MiddlewareError};
use ethers_core::types::{U64, TransactionRequest, U256, transaction::eip2718::TypedTransaction, BlockId};
use thiserror::Error;
use async_trait::async_trait;
#[derive(Debug)]
struct MyMiddleware<M>(M);
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum MyError<M: Middleware> {
    #[error("{0}")]
    MiddlewareError(M::Error),
    // Add your middleware's specific errors here
}
impl<M: Middleware> MiddlewareError for MyError<M> {
    type Inner = M::Error;
    fn from_err(src: M::Error) -> MyError<M> {
        MyError::MiddlewareError(src)
    }
    fn as_inner(&self) -> Option<&Self::Inner> {
        match self {
            MyError::MiddlewareError(e) => Some(e),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}
#[async_trait]
impl<M> Middleware for MyMiddleware<M>
where
    M: Middleware,
{
    type Error = MyError<M>;
    type Provider = M::Provider;
    type Inner = M;
    fn inner(&self) -> &M {
        &self.0
    }
    /// Overrides the default `get_block_number` method to always return 0
    async fn get_block_number(&self) -> Result<U64, Self::Error> {
        Ok(U64::zero())
    }
    /// Overrides the default `estimate_gas` method to log that it was called,
    /// before forwarding the call to the next layer.
    async fn estimate_gas(&self, tx: &TypedTransaction, block: Option<BlockId>) -> Result<U256, Self::Error> {
        println!("Estimating gas...");
        self.inner().estimate_gas(tx, block).await.map_err(MiddlewareError::from_err)
    }
}
```

Fill necessary details of a transaction for dispatch

This function is defined on providers to behave as follows:

- populate the `from`field with the default sender
- resolve any ENS names in the tx `to`field
- Estimate gas usage
- Poll and set legacy or 1559 gas prices
- Set the chain_id with the provider’s, if not already set

It does NOT set the nonce by default.

Middleware are encouraged to override any values *before* delegating
to the inner implementation AND/OR modify the values provided by the
default implementation *after* delegating.

E.g. a middleware wanting to double gas prices should consider doing so
*after* delegating and allowing the default implementation to poll gas.

Send a transaction with a simple escalation policy.

`policy` should be a boxed function that maps `original_gas_price`
and `number_of_previous_escalations` -> `new_gas_price`.

e.g. `Box::new(|start, escalation_index| start * 1250.pow(escalations) / 1000.pow(escalations))`

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use ethers_providers::erc::ERCNFT;
let token = "erc721:0xc92ceddfb8dd984a89fb494c376f9a48b999aafc/9018".parse()?;
let token_image = provider.resolve_nft(token).await?;
assert_eq!(
    token_image.to_string(),
    "https://creature.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/QmNwj3aUzXfG4twV3no7hJRYxLLAWNPk6RrfQaqJ6nVJFa/9018.jpg"
);
```

or IPC. For a polling alternative available over HTTP, use
[ Middleware::watch](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html#method.watch). However, be aware that polling increases
RPC usage drastically.

Trait for signing transactions and messages

Implement this trait to support different signing modes, e.g. Ledger, hosted etc.

# Wallet in ethers::signers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/signers/struct.Wallet.html

`pub struct Wallet<D>{ /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An Ethereum private-public key pair which can be used for signing messages.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#signing-and-verifying-a-message)Signing and Verifying a message

The wallet can be used to produce ECDSA [ Signature](https://docs.rs/core/types/struct.Signature.html) objects, which can be
then verified. Note that this uses

[under the hood which will prefix the message being hashed with the](https://docs.rs/core/utils/fn.hash_message.html)

`hash_message``Ethereum Signed Message` domain separator.```
use ethers_core::rand::thread_rng;
use ethers_signers::{LocalWallet, Signer};
let wallet = LocalWallet::new(&mut thread_rng());
// Optionally, the wallet's chain id can be set, in order to use EIP-155
// replay protection with different chains
let wallet = wallet.with_chain_id(1337u64);
// The wallet can be used to sign messages
let message = b"hello";
let signature = wallet.sign_message(message).await?;
assert_eq!(signature.recover(&message[..]).unwrap(), wallet.address());
// LocalWallet is clonable:
let wallet_clone = wallet.clone();
let signature2 = wallet_clone.sign_message(message).await?;
assert_eq!(signature, signature2);
```

does not specify one.

# abigen in ethers::contract - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/contract/macro.abigen.html

`abigen!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

Generates type-safe bindings to an Ethereum smart contract from its ABI.

All the accepted ABI sources are listed in the examples below and in [Source](https://docs.rs/ethers_contract_abigen::Source).

Note:

- relative paths are rooted in the crate’s root (`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`).
- Environment variable interpolation is supported via `$`prefix, like`"$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/contracts/c.json"`
- Etherscan rate-limits requests to their API. To avoid this, set the `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY`environment variable.

Additionally, this macro accepts additional parameters to configure some aspects of the code generation:

- `methods`: A list of mappings from method signatures to method names allowing methods names to be explicitely set for contract methods. This also provides a workaround for generating code for contracts with multiple methods with the same name.
- `derives`: A list of additional derive macros that are added to all the generated structs and enums, after the default ones which are (- [when applicable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/primitive.tuple.html#trait-implementations-1)):- [PartialEq]
- [Eq]
- [Debug]
- [Default]
- [Hash]

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

All the possible ABI sources:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// ABI Path
abigen!(MyContract, "./MyContractABI.json");
// HTTP(S) source
abigen!(MyContract, "https://my.domain.local/path/to/contract.json");
// Etherscan.io
abigen!(MyContract, "etherscan:0x0001020304050607080910111213141516171819");
abigen!(MyContract, "https://etherscan.io/address/0x0001020304050607080910111213141516171819");
// npmjs
abigen!(MyContract, "npm:@org/package@1.0.0/path/to/contract.json");
// Human readable ABI
abigen!(MyContract, r"[
    function setValue(string)
    function getValue() external view returns (string)
    event ValueChanged(address indexed author, string oldValue, string newValue)
]");
```
Specify additional parameters:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
abigen!(
    MyContract,
    "path/to/MyContract.json",
    methods {
        myMethod(uint256,bool) as my_renamed_method;
    },
    derives(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize),
);
```
Aliases for overloaded functions with no aliases provided in the `method` section are derived
automatically.

`abigen!` supports multiple abigen definitions separated by a semicolon `;`
This is useful if the contracts use ABIEncoderV2 structs. In which case
`abigen!` bundles all type duplicates so that all rust contracts also use
the same rust types.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
abigen!(
    MyContract,
    "path/to/MyContract.json",
    methods {
        myMethod(uint256,bool) as my_renamed_method;
    },
    derives(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize);
    MyOtherContract,
    "path/to/MyOtherContract.json",
    derives(serde::Deserialize, serde::Serialize);
);
```

# ethers::contract - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/contract/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-contract)ethers-contract

Type-safe abstractions for interacting with Ethereum smart contracts.

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

Interacting with a smart contract requires broadcasting carefully crafted
[transactions](https://docs.rs/core/types/struct.TransactionRequest.html) where the `data` field
contains the
[function’s selector](https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/72363/what-is-a-function-selector)
along with the arguments of the called function.

This module provides the [ Contract](https://docs.rs/struct.Contract.html) and

[abstractions so that you do not have to worry about that. It also provides typesafe bindings via the](https://docs.rs/struct.ContractFactory.html)

`ContractFactory`[macro and the](https://docs.rs/macro.abigen.html)

`abigen`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Abigen.html)

`Abigen` builderFor more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [stream](https://docs.rs/stream/index.html)
- Contains the `EventStream`type which aids in streaming access to contract events

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [abigen](https://docs.rs/macro.abigen.html)
- Generates type-safe bindings to an Ethereum smart contract from its ABI.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Abigen](https://docs.rs/struct.Abigen.html)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/struct.Call.html)

- [Contract](https://docs.rs/struct.ContractDeploymentTx.html)- Deployment - Tx
- Helper which manages the deployment transaction of a smart contract. It wraps a deployment transaction, and retrieves the contract address output by it.
- [Contract](https://docs.rs/struct.ContractInstance.html)- Instance
- A Contract is an abstraction of an executable program on the Ethereum Blockchain. It has code (called byte code) as well as allocated long-term memory (called storage). Every deployed Contract has an address, which is used to connect to it so that it may be sent messages to call its methods.
- [Deployment](https://docs.rs/struct.DeploymentTxFactory.html)- TxFactory
- To deploy a contract to the Ethereum network, a `ContractFactory`can be created which manages the Contract bytecode and Application Binary Interface (ABI), usually generated from the Solidity compiler.

- Metadata inside a log

- Collects Abigen structs for a series of contracts, pending generation of the contract bindings.
- [Multicall](https://docs.rs/struct.Multicall.html)
- A Multicall is an abstraction for sending batched calls/transactions to the Ethereum blockchain.
It stores an instance of the `Multicall`smart contract
- [Multicall](https://docs.rs/struct.MulticallContract.html)- Contract
- [Select](https://docs.rs/struct.SelectContracts.html)- Contracts

# ethers::middleware - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/middleware/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-middleware)ethers-middleware

Your ethers application interacts with the blockchain through a [ Provider](https://docs.rs/providers/struct.Provider.html) abstraction.

[is a special type of](https://docs.rs/providers/struct.Provider.html)

`Provider`[that can be composed with others to obtain a layered architecture. This approach promotes “Open Closed Principle”, “Single Responsibility” and composable patterns. The building process happens in a wrapping fashion, and starts from a](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html)

`Middleware`[being the first element in the stack. This process continues having new middlewares being pushed on top of a layered data structure.](https://docs.rs/providers/struct.Provider.html)

`Provider`For more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#available-middleware)Available Middleware

- `Signer`
- `Nonce Manager`
- `Gas Escalator`- `GasEscalatorMiddleware`- [GasEscalator](https://docs.rs/gas_escalator/trait.GasEscalator.html)) and bump frequencies (see- [Frequency](https://docs.rs/gas_escalator/enum.Frequency.html)).
- `Gas Oracle`- `eth_gasPrice`, including REST based gas stations (i.e. Etherscan, ETH Gas Station etc.).
- `Transformer`- `DSProxy`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Each [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html) implements the trait

[MiddlewareBuilder](https://docs.rs/trait.MiddlewareBuilder.html). This trait helps a developer to compose a custom

[stack.](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html)

`Middleware`The following example shows how to build a composed [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html) starting from a

[:](https://docs.rs/providers/struct.Provider.html)

`Provider````
let key = "fdb33e2105f08abe41a8ee3b758726a31abdd57b7a443f470f23efce853af169";
let signer = key.parse::<LocalWallet>()?;
let address = signer.address();
let gas_oracle = GasNow::new();
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from("http://localhost:8545")?
    .gas_oracle(gas_oracle)
    .with_signer(signer)
    .nonce_manager(address); // Outermost layer
```
The [wrap_into](https://docs.rs/trait.MiddlewareBuilder.html#method.wrap_into) function can be used to wrap [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html) layers explicitly. This is useful when pushing

[s not directly handled by the builder interface.](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html)

`Middleware````
let key = "fdb33e2105f08abe41a8ee3b758726a31abdd57b7a443f470f23efce853af169";
let signer = key.parse::<LocalWallet>()?;
let address = signer.address();
let escalator = GeometricGasPrice::new(1.125, 60_u64, None::<u64>);
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from("http://localhost:8545")?
    .wrap_into(|p| GasEscalatorMiddleware::new(p, escalator, Frequency::PerBlock))
    .wrap_into(|p| SignerMiddleware::new(p, signer))
    .wrap_into(|p| GasOracleMiddleware::new(p, GasNow::new()))
    .wrap_into(|p| NonceManagerMiddleware::new(p, address)); // Outermost layer
```
A [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/trait.Middleware.html) stack can be also constructed manually. This is achieved by explicitly wrapping layers.

```
// Start the stack
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from("http://localhost:8545")?;
// Escalate gas prices
let escalator = GeometricGasPrice::new(1.125, 60u64, None::<u64>);
let provider = GasEscalatorMiddleware::new(provider, escalator, Frequency::PerBlock);
// Sign transactions with a private key
let key = "fdb33e2105f08abe41a8ee3b758726a31abdd57b7a443f470f23efce853af169";
let signer = key.parse::<LocalWallet>()?;
let address = signer.address();
let provider = SignerMiddleware::new(provider, signer);
// Use GasNow as the gas oracle
let gas_oracle = GasNow::new();
let provider = GasOracleMiddleware::new(provider, gas_oracle);
// Manage nonces locally
let provider = NonceManagerMiddleware::new(provider, address);
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [builder](https://docs.rs/builder/index.html)
- [MiddlewareBuilder](https://docs.rs/trait.MiddlewareBuilder.html)provides a way to compose many- `Middleware`
- [contract](https://docs.rs/contract/index.html)
- ethers-contract
- [gas_](https://docs.rs/gas_escalator/index.html)- escalator
- The [Gas Escalator middleware](https://docs.rs/struct.GasEscalatorMiddleware.html)is used to re-broadcast transactions with an increasing gas price to guarantee their timely inclusion.
- [gas_](https://docs.rs/gas_oracle/index.html)- oracle
- The gas oracle middleware is used to get the gas price from a list of gas oracles instead of
using `eth_gasPrice`. For usage examples, refer to the`GasOracle`
- [nonce_](https://docs.rs/nonce_manager/index.html)- manager
- The [Nonce Manager](https://docs.rs/struct.NonceManagerMiddleware.html)is used to locally calculate nonces instead of using eth_getTransactionCount
- [policy](https://docs.rs/policy/index.html)
- The [Policy](https://docs.rs/trait.Policy.html)is used to ensure transactions comply with the rules configured in the`PolicyMiddleware`
- [signer](https://docs.rs/signer/index.html)
- The [SignerMiddleware](https://docs.rs/struct.SignerMiddleware.html)is used to locally sign transactions and messages instead of using`eth_sendTransaction`and`eth_sign`.
- [timelag](https://docs.rs/timelag/index.html)
- The [TimeLag](https://docs.rs/struct.TimeLag.html)middleware provides safety against reorgs by querying state N blocks before the chain tip.
- [transformer](https://docs.rs/transformer/index.html)
- The [TransformerMiddleware](https://docs.rs/struct.TransformerMiddleware.html)is used to intercept transactions and transform them to be sent via various supported transformers, e.g.,[DSProxy](https://docs.rs/transformer/struct.DsProxy.html).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Allow](https://docs.rs/struct.AllowEverything.html)- Everything
- A policy that does not restrict anything.
- [GasEscalator](https://docs.rs/struct.GasEscalatorMiddleware.html)- Middleware
- A Gas escalator allows bumping transactions’ gas price to avoid getting them stuck in the memory pool.
- [Nonce](https://docs.rs/struct.NonceManagerMiddleware.html)- Manager - Middleware
- Middleware used for calculating nonces locally, useful for signing multiple consecutive transactions without waiting for them to hit the mempool
- [Policy](https://docs.rs/struct.PolicyMiddleware.html)- Middleware
- Middleware used to enforce certain policies for transactions.
- [Reject](https://docs.rs/struct.RejectEverything.html)- Everything
- A policy that rejects all transactions.
- [Signer](https://docs.rs/struct.SignerMiddleware.html)- Middleware
- Middleware used for locally signing transactions, compatible with any implementer
of the `Signer`
- [TimeLag](https://docs.rs/struct.TimeLag.html)
- TimeLag Provider
- [Transformer](https://docs.rs/struct.TransformerMiddleware.html)- Middleware
- Middleware used for intercepting transaction requests and transforming them to be executed by
the underneath `Transformer`instance.

# ethers::providers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/providers/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-providers)ethers-providers

Clients for interacting with Ethereum nodes.

This crate provides asynchronous
[Ethereum JSON-RPC](https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/JSON-RPC) compliant
clients.

For more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#websockets)Websockets

This crate supports for WebSockets via `tokio-tungstenite`.
Please ensure that you have the `ws` feature enabled if you wish to use WebSockets:

```
[dependencies]
ethers-providers = { version = "2.0", features = ["ws"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#interprocess-communication-ipc)Interprocess Communication (IPC)

This crate supports for Interprocess Communication via Unix sockets and Windows named pipes.
Please ensure that you have the `ipc` feature enabled if you wish to use IPC:

```
[dependencies]
ethers-providers = { version = "2.0", features = ["ipc"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#ethereum-name-service)Ethereum Name Service

The provider may also be used to resolve [Ethereum Name Service](https://ens.domains) (ENS) names
to addresses (and vice versa).
The default ENS address is [ 0x00000000000C2E074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e](https://etherscan.io/address/0x00000000000C2E074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e)
and can be overriden with the

[method on the provider.](https://docs.rs/struct.Provider.html#method.ens)

`ens`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from("https://eth.llamarpc.com")?;
let block = provider.get_block(100u64).await?;
println!("Got block: {}", serde_json::to_string(&block)?);
let addr = "0x89d24a6b4ccb1b6faa2625fe562bdd9a23260359".parse::<Address>()?;
let code = provider.get_code(addr, None).await?;
println!("Got code: {}", serde_json::to_string(&code)?);
```
Using ENS:

```
let provider = Provider::<Http>::try_from("https://eth.llamarpc.com")?;
// Resolve ENS name to Address
let name = "vitalik.eth";
let address = provider.resolve_name(name).await?;
// Lookup ENS name given Address
let resolved_name = provider.lookup_address(address).await?;
assert_eq!(name, resolved_name);
/// Lookup ENS field
let url = "https://vitalik.ca".to_string();
let resolved_url = provider.resolve_field(name, "url").await?;
assert_eq!(url, resolved_url);
/// Lookup and resolve ENS avatar
let avatar = "https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmSP4nq9fnN9dAiCj42ug9Wa79rqmQerZXZch82VqpiH7U/image.gif".to_string();
let resolved_avatar = provider.resolve_avatar(name).await?;
assert_eq!(avatar, resolved_avatar.to_string());
```

- [Pending](https://docs.rs/struct.PendingTransaction.html)- Transaction
- A pending transaction is a transaction which has been submitted but is not yet mined.
`await`’ing on a pending transaction will resolve to a transaction receipt once the transaction has enough`confirmations`. The default number of confirmations is 1, but may be adjusted with the`confirmations`method. If the transaction does not have enough confirmations or is not mined, the future will stay in the pending state.
- [Provider](https://docs.rs/struct.Provider.html)
- An abstract provider for interacting with the [Ethereum JSON RPC API](https://github.com/ethereum/wiki/wiki/JSON-RPC). Must be instantiated with a data transport which implements the`JsonRpcClient`[HTTP](https://docs.rs/struct.Http.html), Websockets etc.)

# ethers::signers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/signers/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-signers)ethers-signers

A unified interface for locally signing Ethereum transactions.

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

You can implement the `Signer` trait to extend functionality to other signers
such as Hardware Security Modules, KMS etc.

The exposed interfaces return a recoverable signature. In order to convert the
signature and the [ TransactionRequest](https://docs.rs/core/types/struct.TransactionRequest.html) to a

[, look at the signing middleware.](https://docs.rs/core/types/struct.Transaction.html)

`Transaction`Supported signers:

For more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
// instantiate the wallet
let wallet = "dcf2cbdd171a21c480aa7f53d77f31bb102282b3ff099c78e3118b37348c72f7"
    .parse::<LocalWallet>()?;
// create a transaction
let tx = TransactionRequest::new()
    .to("vitalik.eth") // this will use ENS
    .value(10000).into();
// sign it
let signature = wallet.sign_transaction(&tx).await?;
// can also sign a message
let signature = wallet.sign_message("hello world").await?;
signature.verify("hello world", wallet.address()).unwrap();
```
Sign an Ethereum prefixed message ([eip-712](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712)):

```
let message = "Some data";
let wallet = LocalWallet::new(&mut rand::thread_rng());
// Sign the message
let signature = wallet.sign_message(message).await?;
// Recover the signer from the message
let recovered = signature.recover(message)?;
assert_eq!(recovered, wallet.address());
```

# ethers::solc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/2.0.14/ethers/solc/index.html

**crate feature**only.

`solc`## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-solc)ethers-solc

Utilities for working with native `solc` and compiling projects.

WarningThis crate is deprecated in favor of

[(](https://crates.io/foundry-compilers)`foundry-compilers`[foundry-rs/compilers](https://github.com/foundry-rs/compilers)). See[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

To also compile contracts during `cargo build` (so that ethers `abigen!` can pull in updated abi automatically) you can configure a `ethers_solc::Project` in your `build.rs` file

First add `ethers-solc` to your cargo build-dependencies.

Once you compiled the project, you can configure cargo change detection with `rerun_if_sources_changed`, so that cargo will execute the `build.rs` file if a contract in the sources directory has changed

```
[build-dependencies]
ethers-solc = { git = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs" }
```
```
use ethers_solc::{Project, ProjectPathsConfig};
fn main() {
    // configure the project with all its paths, solc, cache etc.
    let project = Project::builder()
        .paths(ProjectPathsConfig::hardhat(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).unwrap())
        .build()
        .unwrap();
    let output = project.compile().unwrap();
    // Tell Cargo that if a source file changes, to rerun this build script.
    project.rerun_if_sources_changed();
}
```

# ethers - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ethers/latest/ethers/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#ethers-rs)ethers-rs

A complete Ethereum and Celo Rust library.

[§](https://docs.rs#quickstart-prelude)Quickstart: `prelude`

A prelude is provided which imports all the important data types and traits for you. Use this when you want to quickly bootstrap a new project.

`use ethers::prelude::*;`Examples on how you can use the types imported by the prelude can be found in the
[ examples directory of the repository](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/tree/master/examples)
and in the

`tests/` directories of each crate.[§](https://docs.rs#modules)Modules

The following paragraphs are a quick explanation of each module in ascending order of
abstraction. More details can be found in [the book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#core)`core`

Contains all the [necessary data structures](https://docs.rs/core/types/index.html) for interacting with Ethereum, along
with cryptographic utilities for signing and verifying ECDSA signatures on `secp256k1`. Bindings
to the Solidity compiler, Anvil and Ganace are also provided as helpers.
To simplify your imports, consider using the re-exported modules described in the next
subsection.

[§](https://docs.rs#utils-types-abi)`utils`, `types`, `abi`

These are re-exports of the [ utils](https://docs.rs/core/utils/index.html),

[and](https://docs.rs/core/types/index.html)

`types`[modules from the](https://docs.rs/core/abi/index.html)

`abi`[crate.](https://docs.rs/core/index.html)

`core`[§](https://docs.rs#providers)`providers`

Contains the [ Provider](https://docs.rs/providers/struct.Provider.html) struct, an abstraction of a connection to the Ethereum network, which
alongside the

[trait provides a concise, consistent interface to standard Ethereum node functionality,](https://docs.rs/middleware/trait.Middleware.html)

`Middleware`[§](https://docs.rs#signers)`signers`

Provides a [ Signer](https://docs.rs/signers/trait.Signer.html) trait which can be used for signing messages or transactions. A

[type is implemented which can be used with a raw private key or a YubiHSM2. Ledger and Trezor support are also provided.](https://docs.rs/signers/struct.Wallet.html)

`Wallet`[§](https://docs.rs#contract)`contract`

Interacting with Ethereum is not restricted to sending or receiving funds. It also involves using smart contracts, which can be thought of as programs with persistent storage.

Interacting with a smart contract requires broadcasting carefully crafted
[transactions](https://docs.rs/core/types/struct.TransactionRequest.html) where the `data` field contains
the [function’s
selector](https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/72363/what-is-a-function-selector)
along with the arguments of the called function. This module provides the
[ Contract](https://docs.rs/contract/type.Contract.html) and

[abstractions so that you do not have to worry about that.](https://docs.rs/contract/type.ContractFactory.html)

`ContractFactory`It also provides typesafe bindings via the [ abigen](https://docs.rs/contract/macro.abigen.html) macro and the

[builder.](https://docs.rs/contract/macro.abigen.html)

`Abigen`[§](https://docs.rs#middleware)`middleware`

In order to keep the ethers architecture as modular as possible, providers define a
[ Middleware](https://docs.rs/middleware/trait.Middleware.html) trait which defines all the methods to interact with an Ethereum node. By
implementing the middleware trait, you are able to override the default behavior of methods and
do things such as using other gas oracles, escalating your transactions’ gas prices, or signing
your transactions with a

[. The middleware architecture allows users to either use one of the existing middleware, or they are free to write on of their own.](https://docs.rs/signers/trait.Signer.html)

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |

| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

# ethers-contract 2.0.14 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ethers-contract/^2.0.14

# ethers-contract

Type-safe abstractions for interacting with Ethereum smart contracts.

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

Interacting with a smart contract requires broadcasting carefully crafted
[transactions](https://docs.rs/ethers_core::types::TransactionRequest) where the `data` field
contains the
[function's selector](https://ethereum.stackexchange.com/questions/72363/what-is-a-function-selector)
along with the arguments of the called function.

This module provides the [ Contract](https://docs.rs/struct.Contract.html) and

[abstractions so that you do not have to worry about that. It also provides typesafe bindings via the](https://docs.rs/struct.ContractFactory.html)

`ContractFactory`[macro and the](https://docs.rs/macro.abigen.html)

`abigen`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Abigen.html)

`Abigen` builderFor more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

# ethers-core

Ethereum data types, cryptography and utilities.

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

the `core` module to simplify your imports.

This library provides type definitions for Ethereum's main datatypes along with other utilities for interacting with the Ethereum ecosystem

For more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

[and](https://docs.rs/libsecp256k1)

# use ;

# use utils;
let factory: Address = "0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f".parse?;
let token_a: Address = "0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48".parse?;
let token_b: Address = "0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2".parse?;
let encoded = encode_packed?;
let salt = keccak256;
let init_code_hash: H256 = "0x96e8ac4277198ff8b6f785478aa9a39f403cb768dd02cbee326c3e7da348845f".parse?;
let pair = get_create2_address_from_hash;

# ethers-middleware 2.0.14 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ethers-middleware/^2.0.14

# ethers-middleware

Your ethers application interacts with the blockchain through a [ Provider](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Provider) abstraction.

[is a special type of](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Provider)

`Provider`[that can be composed with others to obtain a layered architecture. This approach promotes "Open Closed Principle", "Single Responsibility" and composable patterns. The building process happens in a wrapping fashion, and starts from a](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware)

`Middleware`[being the first element in the stack. This process continues having new middlewares being pushed on top of a layered data structure.](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Provider)

`Provider`For more information, please refer to the [book](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

## Available Middleware

- `Signer`
- `Nonce Manager`
- `Gas Escalator`- `GasEscalatorMiddleware`- [GasEscalator](crate::gas_escalator::GasEscalator)) and bump frequencies (see- [Frequency](crate::gas_escalator::Frequency)).
- `Gas Oracle`- `eth_gasPrice`, including REST based gas stations (i.e. Etherscan, ETH Gas Station etc.).
- `Transformer`- `DSProxy`

## Examples

Each [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware) implements the trait

[MiddlewareBuilder](crate::MiddlewareBuilder). This trait helps a developer to compose a custom

[stack.](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware)

`Middleware`The following example shows how to build a composed [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware) starting from a

[:](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Provider)

`Provider````
# use ;
# use ;
# use ;
let key = "fdb33e2105f08abe41a8ee3b758726a31abdd57b7a443f470f23efce853af169";
let signer = key.?;
let address = signer.address;
let gas_oracle = new;
let provider = try_from?
    .gas_oracle
    .with_signer
    .nonce_manager; // Outermost layer
# Ok::
```
The [wrap_into](crate::MiddlewareBuilder::wrap_into) function can be used to wrap [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware) layers explicitly. This is useful when pushing

[s not directly handled by the builder interface.](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware)

`Middleware````
# use ;
# use TryFrom;
# use ;
# use ;
let key = "fdb33e2105f08abe41a8ee3b758726a31abdd57b7a443f470f23efce853af169";
let signer = key.?;
let address = signer.address;
let escalator = new;
let provider = try_from?
    .wrap_into
    .wrap_into
    .wrap_into
    .wrap_into; // Outermost layer
# Ok::
```
A [ Middleware](https://docs.rs/ethers_providers::Middleware) stack can be also constructed manually. This is achieved by explicitly wrapping layers.

```
# use ;
# use ;
# use ;
// Start the stack
let provider = try_from?;
// Escalate gas prices
let escalator = new;
let provider = new;
// Sign transactions with a private key
let key = "fdb33e2105f08abe41a8ee3b758726a31abdd57b7a443f470f23efce853af169";
let signer = key.?;
let address = signer.address;
let provider = new;
// Use GasNow as the gas oracle
let gas_oracle = new;
let provider = new;
// Manage nonces locally
let provider = new;
# Ok::
```

# ethers 2.0.13 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ethers/2.0.13

# ethers-rs

**A complete Ethereum and Celo Rust library**

WarningThis library is in the process of being deprecated. See

[#2667](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/2667)for more information.

## Quickstart

Add this to your Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = "2.0"
```
And this to your code:

```
use *;
```
## Documentation

View the API reference [here](https://docs.rs/ethers) or the online book [here](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

Examples are organized into individual crates under the `/examples` folder.
You can run any of the examples by executing:

```
# cargo run -p <example-crate-name> --example <name>
```
## EVM-compatible chains support

There are many chains live which are Ethereum JSON-RPC & EVM compatible, but do not yet have
support for [EIP-2718](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2718) Typed Transactions. This means
that transactions submitted to them by default in ethers-rs will have invalid serialization. To
address that, you must use the `legacy` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["legacy"] }
```
### Polygon support

There is abigen support for Polygon and the Mumbai test network. It is recommended that you set the `POLYGONSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://polygonscan.io/apis).

### Avalanche support

There is abigen support for Avalanche and the Fuji test network. It is recommended that you set the `SNOWTRACE_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://snowtrace.io/apis).

### Optimism support

Optimism is supported via the `optimism` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["optimism"] }
```
Optimism has a new transaction type: [Deposited Transactions](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/specs/deposits.md#the-deposited-transaction-type)
with type ID `0x7E`, which requires 3 new fields:

- `sourceHash`: The hash which uniquely identifies the origin of the deposit
- `mint`: The ETH value to mint on L2.
- `isSystemTx`: True if the tx does not interact with the L2 block gas pool

**Note:** the `optimism` and `celo` features are mutually exclusive.

### Celo Support

[Celo](https://celo.org) support is turned on via the feature-flag `celo`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["celo"] }
```
Celo's transactions differ from Ethereum transactions by including 3 new fields:

- `fee_currency`: The currency fees are paid in (None for CELO, otherwise it's an Address)
- `gateway_fee_recipient`: The address of the fee recipient (None for no gateway fee paid)
- `gateway_fee`: Gateway fee amount (None for no gateway fee paid)

The feature flag enables these additional fields in the transaction request builders and in the transactions which are fetched over JSON-RPC.

**Note:** the `optimism` and `celo` features are mutually exclusive.

## Features

- Ethereum JSON-RPC Client
- Interacting and deploying smart contracts
- Type safe smart contract bindings code generation
- Querying past events
-  Event monitoring as `Stream`s
- ENS as a first class citizen
- Celo support
- Polygon support
- Avalanche support
- Optimism support
-  Websockets / `eth_subscribe`
- Hardware Wallet Support
-  Parity APIs (`tracing`,`parity_blockWithReceipts`)
- Geth TxPool API
- WASM Bindings (see note)
- FFI Bindings (see note)
- CLI for common operations

### Websockets

Websockets support is turned on via the feature-flag `ws`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["ws"] }
```
### Interprocess Communication (IPC)

IPC support is turned on via the feature-flag `ipc`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["ipc"] }
```
### HTTP Secure (HTTPS)

If you are looking to connect to a HTTPS endpoint, then you need to enable the `rustls` or `openssl` feature.
feature-flags.

To enable `rustls`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["rustls"] }
```
To enable `openssl`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["openssl"] }
```
## Note on WASM and FFI bindings

You should be able to build a wasm app that uses ethers-rs (see the [example](https://docs.rs/examples/wasm) for reference).
If ethers fails to compile in WASM, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide an official JS/TS-accessible library
interface, as we believe [viem](https://viem.sh) or [ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.io/v6/)
serve that need very well.

Similarly, you should be able to build FFI bindings to ethers-rs. If ethers
fails to compile in C library formats, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide official FFI bindings.

## Getting Help

First, see if the answer to your question can be found in the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/ethers). If the answer
is not there, try opening an [issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new) with the question.

Join the [ethers-rs telegram](https://t.me/ethers_rs) to chat with the community!

## Contributing

Thanks for your help improving the project! We are so happy to have you! We have
[a contributing guide](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md) to help you get involved in the ethers-rs project.

If you open a Pull Request, do not forget to add your changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://docs.rs/CHANGELOG.md), ensure your code is
properly formatted with `cargo +nightly fmt` and that Clippy is happy `cargo clippy`; you can even try to let clippy fix simple
issues itself: `cargo +nightly clippy --fix`

## Projects using ethers-rs

- [Yield Liquidator](https://github.com/yieldprotocol/yield-liquidator/): Liquidator for Yield Protocol
- [MEV Inspect](https://github.com/flashbots/mev-inspect-rs/): Miner Extractable Value inspector
- [Ethers CCIP-Read](https://github.com/ensdomains/ethers-ccip-read): Ethers middleware for ENS- [CCIP-Read](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3668)support
- [Ethers Flashbots](https://github.com/onbjerg/ethers-flashbots): Ethers middleware for- [Flashbots](https://docs.flashbots.net)
- [Ethers Fireblocks](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-fireblocks): Ethers middleware and signer for- [Fireblocks](https://fireblocks.io)' API
- [Celo Threshold BLS DKG](https://github.com/celo-org/celo-threshold-bls-rs/): CLI for using Celo as a data availability network for the Joint-Feldman BLS DKG
- [Celo Plumo Prover](https://github.com/celo-org/plumo-prover): Creates Celo's ultralight client proof from on-chain data
- [Celo SNARK Setup Coordinator](https://github.com/celo-org/snark-setup-operator): Coordinator for executing a pipelined Groth16 SNARK setup
- [ERC-4337 Bundler](https://github.com/Vid201/aa-bundler/): Account Abstraction (ERC-4337) bundler
- [zkSync Withdrawal Finalizer](https://github.com/matter-labs/zksync-withdrawal-finalizer): Finalizer of withdrawals from zkSync Era to L1.

# ethers 2.0.10 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ethers/2.0.10

# ethers-rs

**A complete Ethereum and Celo Rust library**

## Quickstart

Add this to your Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = "2.0"
```
And this to your code:

```
use *;
```
## Documentation

View the API reference [here](https://docs.rs/ethers) or the online book [here](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

Examples are organized into individual crates under the `/examples` folder.
You can run any of the examples by executing:

```
# cargo run -p <example-crate-name> --example <name>
```
## EVM-compatible chains support

There are many chains live which are Ethereum JSON-RPC & EVM compatible, but do not yet have
support for [EIP-2718](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2718) Typed Transactions. This means
that transactions submitted to them by default in ethers-rs will have invalid serialization. To
address that, you must use the `legacy` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["legacy"] }
```
### Polygon support

There is abigen support for Polygon and the Mumbai test network. It is recommended that you set the `POLYGONSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://polygonscan.io/apis).

### Avalanche support

There is abigen support for Avalanche and the Fuji test network. It is recommended that you set the `SNOWTRACE_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://snowtrace.io/apis).

### Optimism support

Optimism is supported via the `optimism` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["optimism"] }
```
Optimism has a new transaction type: [Deposited Transactions](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/specs/deposits.md#the-deposited-transaction-type)
with type ID `0x7E`, which requires 3 new fields:

- `sourceHash`: The hash which uniquely identifies the origin of the deposit
- `mint`: The ETH value to mint on L2.
- `isSystemTx`: True if the tx does not interact with the L2 block gas pool

**Note:** the `optimism` and `celo` features are mutually exclusive.

### Celo Support

[Celo](https://celo.org) support is turned on via the feature-flag `celo`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["celo"] }
```
Celo's transactions differ from Ethereum transactions by including 3 new fields:

- `fee_currency`: The currency fees are paid in (None for CELO, otherwise it's an Address)
- `gateway_fee_recipient`: The address of the fee recipient (None for no gateway fee paid)
- `gateway_fee`: Gateway fee amount (None for no gateway fee paid)

The feature flag enables these additional fields in the transaction request builders and in the transactions which are fetched over JSON-RPC.

**Note:** the `optimism` and `celo` features are mutually exclusive.

## Features

- Ethereum JSON-RPC Client
- Interacting and deploying smart contracts
- Type safe smart contract bindings code generation
- Querying past events
-  Event monitoring as `Stream`s
- ENS as a first class citizen
- Celo support
- Polygon support
- Avalanche support
- Optimism support
-  Websockets / `eth_subscribe`
- Hardware Wallet Support
-  Parity APIs (`tracing`,`parity_blockWithReceipts`)
- Geth TxPool API
- WASM Bindings (see note)
- FFI Bindings (see note)
- CLI for common operations

### Websockets

Websockets support is turned on via the feature-flag `ws`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["ws"] }
```
### Interprocess Communication (IPC)

IPC support is turned on via the feature-flag `ipc`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["ipc"] }
```
### HTTP Secure (HTTPS)

If you are looking to connect to a HTTPS endpoint, then you need to enable the `rustls` or `openssl` feature.
feature-flags.

To enable `rustls`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["rustls"] }
```
To enable `openssl`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["openssl"] }
```
## Note on WASM and FFI bindings

You should be able to build a wasm app that uses ethers-rs (see the [example](https://docs.rs/examples/wasm) for reference).
If ethers fails to compile in WASM, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide an official JS/TS-accessible library
interface, as we believe [viem](https://viem.sh) or [ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.io/v6/)
serve that need very well.

Similarly, you should be able to build FFI bindings to ethers-rs. If ethers
fails to compile in C library formats, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide official FFI bindings.

Join the [ethers-rs telegram](https://t.me/ethers_rs) to chat with the community!

Optimism has a new transaction type: [Deposited Transactions](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/specs/deposits.md#the-deposited-transaction-type)
with type ID `0x7E`, which requires 3 new fields:

- `sourceHash`: The hash which uniquely identifies the origin of the deposit
- `mint`: The ETH value to mint on L2.
- `isSystemTx`: True if the tx does not interact with the L2 block gas pool

**Note:** the `optimism` and `celo` features are mutually exclusive.

### Celo Support

[Celo](https://celo.org) support is turned on via the feature-flag `celo`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["celo"] }
```
Celo's transactions differ from Ethereum transactions by including 3 new fields:

- `fee_currency`: The currency fees are paid in (None for CELO, otherwise it's an Address)
- `gateway_fee_recipient`: The address of the fee recipient (None for no gateway fee paid)
- `gateway_fee`: Gateway fee amount (None for no gateway fee paid)

The feature flag enables these additional fields in the transaction request builders and in the transactions which are fetched over JSON-RPC.

**Note:** the `optimism` and `celo` features are mutually exclusive.

## Features

- Ethereum JSON-RPC Client
- Interacting and deploying smart contracts
- Type safe smart contract bindings code generation
- Querying past events
-  Event monitoring as `Stream`s
- ENS as a first class citizen
- Celo support
- Polygon support
- Avalanche support
- Optimism support
-  Websockets / `eth_subscribe`
- Hardware Wallet Support
-  Parity APIs (`tracing`,`parity_blockWithReceipts`)
- Geth TxPool API
- WASM Bindings (see note)
- FFI Bindings (see note)
- CLI for common operations

### Websockets

Websockets support is turned on via the feature-flag `ws`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["ws"] }
```
### Interprocess Communication (IPC)

IPC support is turned on via the feature-flag `ipc`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["ipc"] }
```
### HTTP Secure (HTTPS)

If you are looking to connect to a HTTPS endpoint, then you need to enable the `rustls` or `openssl` feature.
feature-flags.

To enable `rustls`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["rustls"] }
```
To enable `openssl`:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["openssl"] }
```
## Note on WASM and FFI bindings

You should be able to build a wasm app that uses ethers-rs (see the [example](https://docs.rs/examples/wasm) for reference).
If ethers fails to compile in WASM, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide an official JS/TS-accessible library
interface, as we believe [viem](https://viem.sh) or [ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.io/v6/)
serve that need very well.

Similarly, you should be able to build FFI bindings to ethers-rs. If ethers
fails to compile in C library formats, please [open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide official FFI bindings.

## Getting Help

First, see if the answer to your question can be found in the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/ethers). If the answer
is not there, try opening an [issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new) with the question.

Join the [ethers-rs telegram](https://t.me/ethers_rs) to chat with the community!

# ethers-rs

**A complete Ethereum and Celo Rust library**

[]
 = "2.0"

use *;

Examples are organized into individual crates under the `/examples` folder.
You can run any of the examples by executing:

```
# cargo run -p <example-crate-name> --example <name>
```
## EVM-compatible chains support

There are many chains live which are Ethereum JSON-RPC & EVM compatible, but do not yet have
support for [EIP-2718](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2718) Typed Transactions. This means
that transactions submitted to them by default in ethers-rs will have invalid serialization. To
address that, you must use the `legacy` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "2.0",  = ["legacy"] }
```
### Polygon support

There is abigen support for Polygon and the Mumbai test network. It is recommended that you set the `POLYGONSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://polygonscan.io/apis).

### Avalanche support

There is abigen support for Avalanche and the Fuji test network. It is recommended that you set the `SNOWTRACE_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://snowtrace.io/apis).

### Optimism support

Optimism is supported via the `optimism` feature flag:

```

use *;
```
## Documentation

View the API reference [here](https://docs.rs/ethers) or the online book [here](https://gakonst.com/ethers-rs).

Examples are organized into individual crates under the `/examples` folder.
You can run any of the examples by executing:

```
# cargo run -p <example-crate-name> --example <name>
```
## EVM-compatible chains support

There are many chains live which are Ethereum JSON-RPC & EVM compatible, but do not yet have
support for [EIP-2718](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2718) Typed Transactions. This means
that transactions submitted to them by default in ethers-rs will have invalid serialization. To
address that, you must use the `legacy` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.2",  = ["legacy"] }
```
### Polygon support

There is abigen support for Polygon and the Mumbai test network. It is recommended that you set the `POLYGONSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://polygonscan.io/apis).

### Avalanche support

There is abigen support for Avalanche and the Fuji test network. It is recommended that you set the `SNOWTRACE_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://snowtrace.io/apis).

### Celo Support

[Celo](https://celo.org) support is turned on via the feature-flag `celo`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.2",  = ["celo"] }
```
Celo's transactions differ from Ethereum transactions by including 3 new fields:

- `fee_currency`: The currency fees are paid in (None for CELO, otherwise it's an Address)
- `gateway_fee_recipient`: The address of the fee recipient (None for no gateway fee paid)
- `gateway_fee`: Gateway fee amount (None for no gateway fee paid)

The feature flag enables these additional fields in the transaction request builders and in the transactions which are fetched over JSON-RPC.

## Features

- Ethereum JSON-RPC Client
- Interacting and deploying smart contracts
- Type safe smart contract bindings code generation
- Querying past events
-  Event monitoring as `Stream`s
- ENS as a first class citizen
- Celo support
- Polygon support
- Avalanche support
-  Websockets / `eth_subscribe`
- Hardware Wallet Support
-  Parity APIs (`tracing`,`parity_blockWithReceipts`)
- Geth TxPool API
- WASM Bindings (see note)
- FFI Bindings (see note)
- CLI for common operations

### Websockets

Websockets support is turned on via the feature-flag `ws`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.2",  = ["ws"] }
```
### Interprocess Communication (IPC)

IPC support is turned on via the feature-flag `ipc`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.2",  = ["ipc"] }
```
### HTTP Secure (HTTPS)

If you are looking to connect to a HTTPS endpoint, then you need to enable the `rustls` or `openssl` feature.
feature-flags.

To enable `rustls`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.2",  = ["rustls"] }
```
To enable `openssl`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.2",  = ["openssl"] }
```
## Note on WASM and FFI bindings

You should be able to build a wasm app that uses ethers-rs (see the [example](https://docs.rs/examples/wasm) for reference). If ethers fails to
compile in WASM, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide an official JS/TS-accessible library
interface. we believe [ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.io/v5/) serves that need
very well.

Similarly, you should be able to build FFI bindings to ethers-rs. If ethers
fails to compile in c lib formats, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide official FFI bindings, and as ethers-rs is
not yet stable 1.0.0, its interface may change significantly between versions.

## Getting Help

First, see if the answer to your question can be found in the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/ethers). If the answer
is not there, try opening an [issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new) with the question.

Join the [ethers-rs telegram](https://t.me/ethers_rs) to chat with the community!

properly formatted with `cargo +nightly fmt` and that Clippy is happy `cargo clippy`; you can even try to let clippy fix simple
issues itself: `cargo +nightly clippy --fix`

[here](https://etherscan.io/apis).

## Projects using ethers-rs

- [Yield Liquidator](https://github.com/yieldprotocol/yield-liquidator/): Liquidator for Yield Protocol
- [MEV Inspect](https://github.com/flashbots/mev-inspect-rs/): Miner Extractable Value inspector
- [Ethers Flashbots](https://github.com/onbjerg/ethers-flashbots): Ethers middleware for- [Flashbots](https://docs.flashbots.net)
- [Ethers Fireblocks](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-fireblocks): Ethers middleware and signer for- [Fireblocks](https://fireblocks.io)' API
- [Celo Threshold BLS DKG](https://github.com/celo-org/celo-threshold-bls-rs/): CLI for using Celo as a data availability network for the Joint-Feldman BLS DKG
- [Celo Plumo Prover](https://github.com/celo-org/plumo-prover): Creates Celo's ultralight client proof from on-chain data
- [Celo SNARK Setup Coordinator](https://github.com/celo-org/snark-setup-operator): Coordinator for executing a pipelined Groth16 SNARK setup

## Documentation

Extensive documentation and examples are available [here](https://docs.rs/ethers).

Alternatively, you may clone the repository and run `cd ethers/ && cargo doc --open`

You can also run any of the examples by executing: `cargo run -p ethers --example <name>`

## Add ethers-rs to your repository

```
[]
 = "1.0.0"
```
## Running the tests

Tests require the following installed:

- `solc`- [solc-select](https://github.com/crytic/solc-select)for more flexibility.
- `anvil`
- `geth`

In addition, it is recommended that you set the `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable
for [the abigen via Etherscan](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/blob/master/ethers-contract/tests/abigen.rs) tests.
You can get one [here](https://etherscan.io/apis).

### EVM-compatible chains support

There are many chains live which are Ethereum JSON-RPC & EVM compatible, but do not yet have
support for [EIP-2718](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2718) Typed Transactions. This means
that transactions submitted to them by default in ethers-rs will have invalid serialization. To
address that, you must use the `legacy` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.0",  = ["legacy"] }
```
### Polygon support

There is abigen support for Polygon and the Mumbai test network. It is recommended that you set the `POLYGONSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://polygonscan.io/apis).

### Avalanche support

There is abigen support for Avalanche and the Fuji test network. It is recommended that you set the `SNOWTRACE_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://snowtrace.io/apis).

### Celo Support

[Celo](http://celo.org/) support is turned on via the feature-flag `celo`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.0",  = ["celo"] }
```
Celo's transactions differ from Ethereum transactions by including 3 new fields:

- `fee_currency`: The currency fees are paid in (None for CELO, otherwise it's an Address)
- `gateway_fee_recipient`: The address of the fee recipient (None for no gateway fee paid)
- `gateway_fee`: Gateway fee amount (None for no gateway fee paid)

The feature flag enables these additional fields in the transaction request builders and in the transactions which are fetched over JSON-RPC.

## Features

- Ethereum JSON-RPC Client
- Interacting and deploying smart contracts
- Type safe smart contract bindings code generation
- Querying past events
-  Event monitoring as `Stream`s
- ENS as a first class citizen
- Celo support
- Polygon support
- Avalanche support
-  Websockets / `eth_subscribe`
- Hardware Wallet Support
-  Parity APIs (`tracing`,`parity_blockWithReceipts`)
- Geth TxPool API
- WASM Bindings (see note)
- FFI Bindings (see note)
- CLI for common operations

### Websockets

Websockets support is turned on via the feature-flag `ws`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.0",  = ["ws"] }
```
### Interprocess Communication (IPC)

IPC support is turned on via the feature-flag `ipc`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.0",  = ["ipc"] }
```
### HTTP Secure (HTTPS)

If you are looking to connect to a HTTPS endpoint, then you need to enable the `rustls` or `openssl` feature.
feature-flags.

To enable `rustls`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.0",  = ["rustls"] }
```
To enable `openssl`:

```
[]
 = {  = "1.0.0",  = ["openssl"] }
```
## Note on WASM and FFI bindings

You should be able to build a wasm app that uses ethers-rs (see the [example](https://docs.rs/examples/ethers-wasm) for reference). If ethers fails to
compile in WASM, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide an official JS/TS-accessible library
interface. we believe [ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.io/v5/) serves that need
very well.

Similarly, you should be able to build FFI bindings to ethers-rs. If ethers
fails to compile in c lib formats, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide official FFI bindings, and as ethers-rs is
not yet stable 1.0.0, its interface may change significantly between versions.

## Getting Help

First, see if the answer to your question can be found in the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/ethers). If the answer
is not there, try opening an [issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new) with the question.

Join the [ethers-rs telegram](https://t.me/ethers_rs) to chat with the community!

## Contributing

Thanks for your help improving the project! We are so happy to have you! We have
[a contributing guide](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) to
help you get involved in the ethers-rs project.

If you make a Pull Request, do not forget to add your changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://docs.rs/CHANGELOG.md) and ensure your code is
properly formatted with `cargo +nightly fmt` and clippy is happy `cargo clippy`, you can even try to let clippy fix simple
issues itself: `cargo +nightly clippy --fix -Z unstable-options`

## Related Projects

This library would not have been possible without the great work done in:

A lot of the code was inspired and adapted from them, to a unified and opinionated interface, built with async/await and std futures from the ground up.

## Projects using ethers-rs

- [Yield Liquidator](https://github.com/yieldprotocol/yield-liquidator/): Liquidator for Yield Protocol
- [MEV Inspect](https://github.com/flashbots/mev-inspect-rs/): Miner Extractable Value inspector
- [Ethers Flashbots](https://github.com/onbjerg/ethers-flashbots): Ethers middleware for- [Flashbots](https://docs.flashbots.net)
- [Ethers Fireblocks](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-fireblocks): Ethers middleware and signer for- [Fireblocks](https://fireblocks.io)' API
- [Celo Threshold BLS DKG](https://github.com/celo-org/celo-threshold-bls-rs/): CLI for using Celo as a data availability network for the Joint-Feldman BLS DKG
- [Celo Plumo Prover](https://github.com/celo-org/plumo-prover): Creates Celo's ultralight client proof from on-chain data
- [Celo SNARK Setup Coordinator](https://github.com/celo-org/snark-setup-operator): Coordinator for executing a pipelined Groth16 SNARK setup

# ethers.rs

**Complete Ethereum and Celo wallet implementation and utilities in Rust**

## Documentation

Extensive documentation and examples are available [here](https://docs.rs/ethers).

Alternatively, you may clone the repository and run `cd ethers/ && cargo doc --open`

You can also run any of the examples by executing: `cargo run -p ethers --example <name>`

## Add ethers-rs to your repository

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs" }
```
## Running the tests

Tests require the following installed:

- `solc`- [solc-select](https://github.com/crytic/solc-select)for more flexibility.
- `anvil`
- `geth`

In addition, it is recommended that you set the `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable
for [the abigen via Etherscan](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/blob/master/ethers-contract/tests/abigen.rs) tests.
You can get one [here](https://etherscan.io/apis).

### EVM-compatible chains support

There are many chains live which are Ethereum JSON-RPC & EVM compatible, but do not yet have
support for [EIP-2718](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2718) Typed Transactions. This means
that transactions submitted to them by default in ethers-rs will have invalid serialization. To
address that, you must use the `legacy` feature flag:

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs",  = ["legacy"] }
```
### Polygon support

There is abigen support for Polygon and the Mumbai test network. It is recommended that you set the `POLYGONSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://polygonscan.io/apis).

### Avalanche support

There is abigen support for Avalanche and the Fuji test network. It is recommended that you set the `SNOWTRACE_API_KEY` environment variable.
You can get one [here](https://snowtrace.io/apis).

### Celo Support

[Celo](http://celo.org/) support is turned on via the feature-flag `celo`:

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs",  = ["celo"] }
```
Celo's transactions differ from Ethereum transactions by including 3 new fields:

- `fee_currency`: The currency fees are paid in (None for CELO, otherwise it's an Address)
- `gateway_fee_recipient`: The address of the fee recipient (None for no gateway fee paid)
- `gateway_fee`: Gateway fee amount (None for no gateway fee paid)

The feature flag enables these additional fields in the transaction request builders and in the transactions which are fetched over JSON-RPC.

## Features

- Ethereum JSON-RPC Client
- Interacting and deploying smart contracts
- Type safe smart contract bindings code generation
- Querying past events
-  Event monitoring as `Stream`s
- ENS as a first class citizen
- Celo support
- Polygon support
- Avalanche support
-  Websockets / `eth_subscribe`
- Hardware Wallet Support
-  Parity APIs (`tracing`,`parity_blockWithReceipts`)
- Geth TxPool API
- WASM Bindings (see note)
- FFI Bindings (see note)
- CLI for common operations

### Websockets

Websockets support is turned on via the feature-flag `ws`:

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs",  = ["ws"] }
```
### Interprocess Communication (IPC)

IPC support is turned on via the feature-flag `ipc`:

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs",  = ["ipc"] }
```
### HTTP Secure (HTTPS)

If you are looking to connect to a HTTPS endpoint, then you need to enable the `rustls` or `openssl` feature.
feature-flags.

To enable `rustls`:

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs",  = ["rustls"] }
```
To enable `openssl`:

```
[]
 = {  = "https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs",  = ["openssl"] }
```
## Note on WASM and FFI bindings

You should be able to build a wasm app that uses ethers-rs (see the [example](https://docs.rs/examples/ethers-wasm) for reference). If ethers fails to
compile in WASM, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide an official JS/TS-accessible library
interface. we believe [ethers.js](https://docs.ethers.io/v5/) serves that need
very well.

Similarly, you should be able to build FFI bindings to ethers-rs. If ethers
fails to compile in c lib formats, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new/choose).
There is currently no plan to provide official FFI bindings, and as ethers-rs is
not yet stable 1.0.0, its interface may change significantly between versions.

## Getting Help

First, see if the answer to your question can be found in the [API documentation](https://docs.rs/ethers). If the answer
is not there, try opening an [issue](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/issues/new) with the question.

Join the [ethers-rs telegram](https://t.me/ethers_rs) to chat with the community!

## Contributing

Thanks for your help improving the project! We are so happy to have you! We have
[a contributing guide](https://github.com/gakonst/ethers-rs/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) to
help you get involved in the ethers-rs project.

If you make a Pull Request, do not forget to add your changes in the [CHANGELOG](https://docs.rs/CHANGELOG.md) and ensure your code if
properly formatted with `cargo +nightly fmt` and clippy is happy `cargo clippy`, you can even try to let clippy fix simple
issues itself: `cargo +nightly clippy --fix -Z unstable-options`

## Related Projects

A lot of the code was inspired and adapted from them, to a unified and opinionated interface, built with async/await and std futures from the ground up.

- [Celo SNARK Setup Coordinator](https://github.com/celo-org/snark-setup-operator): Coordinator for executing a pipelined Groth16 SNARK setup
